body.statement: For fixed identified within-arm margins, \(\Theta_I(P)\) is compact and convex in the uniform norm on \(\mathcal H_\eta\), every continuous signed support functional is attained, and the interpolated exact grid surface sets from nested meshes converge to \(\Theta_I(P)\) in Hausdorff distance. Consequently their support values and sharp fixed-cohort RM integrals converge to the continuous-support values.
body.justification: Continuous-time conclusions require more than solving unrelated finite grids; compactness and Hausdorff convergence transfer exact support certificates to the scientific time scale.
body.gap: Generic optimal-transport consistency does not address strict within-arm event order, a nested survivor denominator, or uniform convergence of a two-index surface image.
body.consumer: It justifies refining the clinical horizon grid without changing the estimand or losing sharpness.
body.proof_tex:
The proof uses weak compactness, a common modulus, and two-sided approximation of feasible fibers.  Fix the identified within-arm margins.  For each \(x\), let \(\mathcal Q_x\) be the full-law fiber with these margins and support on \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  The compact-carrier lemma makes the ambient probability-law space weakly compact.  Marginalization is weakly continuous, and the monotonicity relation is closed; hence \(\mathcal Q_x\) is closed and compact.  The strict within-arm event order causes no closure problem because every law in the fiber has the same fixed margins, each supported on the semicompeting-risk set.  The capacity-projection theorem identifies the \((D(0),R(1))\)-projection of \(\mathcal Q_x\) with \(\mathcal N_x\).  Therefore every \(\mathcal N_x\), and their finite product over \(\mathcal X\), is compact and convex.

For \(r,r',t,t'\in[0,\tau]\) and \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\), the fixed death and readmission margins imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left|\nu_x((t,\infty]\times[0,r])
-\nu_x((t',\infty]\times[0,r'])\right|\\
&\qquad\leq d_x((t\wedge t',t\vee t'])
+\zeta_x((r\wedge r',r\vee r'])
\leq M(|t-t'|+|r-r'|).                                                \tag{26}
\end{aligned}
\]
The density envelope gives the analogous bound for \(b_x\), and \(|S(t)-S(t')|\leq M|t-t'|\).  On \(\mathcal H_\eta\), \(S\geq\eta>0\), while every numerator is bounded in absolute value by one.  Thus
\[
 \left|\frac{N}{S}-\frac{N'}{S'}\right|
 \leq\frac{|N-N'|}{\eta}
 +\frac{|N'|\,|S-S'|}{\eta^2}                                       \tag{27}
\]
gives one Lipschitz modulus for all \(\theta_\nu\).  The same density bound makes \(S\) continuous, so the target-domain definition makes \(\mathcal H_\eta\) a closed subset of the compact time triangle.  Integrating the common TV modulus gives a common modulus for \(\rho_\nu\).

If \(\nu_x^{(q)}\Rightarrow\nu_x\), each finite threshold rectangle in the surface formula is a continuity set because the fixed finite-part death and readmission margins have densities.  Hence \(\theta_{\nu^{(q)}}\to\theta_\nu\) pointwise.  Equation (27) and a finite net of the compact target domain upgrade pointwise convergence to uniform convergence.  The RM integral then converges uniformly as well.  Thus the surface map is continuous from a compact fiber into \(C(\mathcal H_\eta)^2\).  Its image \(\Theta_I(P)\) is compact.  It is convex because the TV numerator and RM integral are affine in \(\nu\), while \(S\) and \(b_x\) are fixed.  Every continuous linear signed support functional therefore attains both extrema.

Now take nested partitions of mesh \(\delta_m\downarrow0\) that isolate \(\infty\), round finite death coordinates monotonically upward, retain within-bin event-order labels, and use one fixed multilinear interpolation on the triangular domain.  Let \(K_m\) be the exact chain-flow surface image for the coarsened fixed margins and let \(K=\Theta_I(P)\).  For any \(Q\in\prod_x\mathcal Q_x\), coarsening all finite coordinates preserves every suffix capacity because \(D(0)>u\) still implies \(D(1)>u\).  At grid knots the coarsened and continuous numerators can differ only on boundary strips of width at most \(\delta_m\), whose marginal probability is at most \(M\delta_m\) per coordinate.  Upward death rounding gives a coarsened survivor denominator no smaller than \(S\), and its difference from \(S\) is at most \(M\delta_m\).  Equation (27) and interpolation therefore give a constant \(C=C(M,\eta,\tau,|\mathcal X|)\) such that
\[
 \sup_{q\in K}\inf_{q_m\in K_m}\|q-q_m\|_\infty
 \leq C\delta_m\longrightarrow0.                                   \tag{28}
\]

Conversely, take \(q_m\in K_m\) and use the quadratic chain theorem to lift its grid flow to a finite-grid full law.  Embed every finite category at a legal representative in its cell, using the retained order label when two events share a cell.  The embedded within-arm margins converge weakly to the fixed margins.  Grid monotonicity gives \(D_m(0)\leq D_m(1)+\delta_m\), so every weak subsequential limit is supported on the closed relation \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  Compactness supplies such a subsequence, and its limit lies in \(\prod_x\mathcal Q_x\).

Every finite grid atom is bounded by the fixed marginal mass of one mesh cell and hence by \(M\delta_m\).  The interpolated grid surfaces therefore obey the common modulus (26)--(27), up to a term vanishing with \(\delta_m\).  Pointwise convergence at continuity thresholds and the finite-net argument show that the chosen subsequence converges uniformly to the surface of its limiting compatible law.  If the reverse directed distance did not vanish, a countersequence attaining a positive lower bound and this subsequence construction would contradict that bound.  Hence
\[
 \sup_{q_m\in K_m}\inf_{q\in K}\|q_m-q\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.    \tag{29}
\]
Equations (28)--(29) prove \(d_H(K_m,K)\to0\).

For every continuous linear functional \(L\),
\[
 \left|\sup_{q_m\in K_m}L(q_m)-\sup_{q\in K}L(q)\right|
 \leq\|L\|\,d_H(K_m,K)\longrightarrow0.                            \tag{30}
\]
The fixed-cohort theorem expresses the sharp RM endpoints as integrals of common sharp TV envelopes.  Their common modulus and Hausdorff convergence yield uniform convergence of those envelopes, so
\[
 \left|\int_0^a\theta_m^{U,L}(r,t)\,dr
-\int_0^a\theta^{U,L}(r,t)\,dr\right|
\leq a\,\|\theta_m^{U,L}-\theta^{U,L}\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus exact grid supports and sharp fixed-cohort RM integrals converge to their continuous-support counterparts.
